Sexuality

Sexuality — sexual health across lifespan, illness effects, and nurse's role in discussing sexuality.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Define sexuality and its components
  • Describe how illness affects sexuality
  • Explain the nurse's role in supporting sexual health

In simple words

Sexuality is a core part of being human — it includes gender identity, sexual orientation, intimacy, relationships and reproduction. It continues throughout life, including during illness and older age.

Illness, surgery, medicines and hospitalisation can affect sexuality. Nurses should address sexuality with respect, privacy and without judgement.

Sexuality across the lifespan

Stage Focus
Childhood Learning about body and privacy
Adolescence Puberty, identity, relationships
Adulthood Intimacy, reproduction, relationships
Older age Continued intimacy; may need adaptation

Effects of illness on sexuality

  • Surgery (mastectomy, hysterectomy, prostate surgery) — body image changes.
  • Medicines — may reduce libido or cause erectile dysfunction.
  • Pain, fatigue and anxiety — reduce sexual interest.
  • Disability — may need positioning aids or new ways of intimacy.

Nurse’s role

  • Provide privacy for couples.
  • Answer questions honestly and respectfully.
  • Do not assume all patients are heterosexual — avoid assumptions.
  • Refer to counsellors or doctors when needed.
  • Keep information confidential.

🔴 Respect and privacy

Treat sexuality with respect and privacy. Do not make assumptions about a patient’s orientation or activity; keep all discussions confidential.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Privacy — provide privacy for married couples; knock before entering.
  • Assessment — ask about sexual health concerns when relevant; do not judge.
  • Education — give information on safe sex, contraception or sexual changes after illness.
  • Referral — refer to doctors or counsellors for sexual problems.
  • Confidentiality — never discuss a patient’s sexual matters with others.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Sexuality includes gender identity, orientation, intimacy, relationships and reproduction.
  2. Sexuality continues throughout life, including illness and older age.
  3. Illness, surgery and medicines can affect sexual function and body image.
  4. Provide privacy and treat sexuality with respect and confidentiality.
  5. Do not assume all patients are heterosexual.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Older adults continue to have sexual needs.
  2. Some medicines reduce libido; discuss with the doctor.
  3. Refer to counsellors for sexual concerns.
  4. Knock before entering; provide privacy for couples.

📌 Memory trick

Sexuality respect: “P-R-C” — Privacy, Respect, Confidentiality.

60-second revision

  • Sexuality = gender identity, orientation, intimacy, relationships, reproduction.
  • Continues throughout life.
  • Illness/surgery/medicines can affect it.
  • Nurse: privacy, respect, confidentiality, no assumptions.
  • Refer to counsellors/doctors for sexual concerns.

Test yourself

Sexuality includes:

Answer: B. Sexuality includes gender identity, sexual orientation, intimacy, relationships and reproduction.

Older adults:

Answer: B. Sexuality continues in older age; older adults have sexual needs.

The nurse should NOT:

Answer: B. Do not assume a patient’s sexual orientation — ask respectfully if relevant.

Which medicine effect may affect sexuality?

Answer: B. Some medicines reduce libido or cause erectile dysfunction.

For a married couple in hospital, the nurse should:

Answer: B. Provide privacy — knock before entering and respect the couple’s relationship.
